proposals.before: When Murong De summoned him, he slipped away without a word to mother or wife.
proposals.after: When Murong De summoned him, he slipped away without a word to mother and wife.
proposals.reason: Chinese 母妻 means mother and wife together, not exclusive ‘or’.

proposals.before: Murong De named him Chao, made him Prince of Beihai, palace attendant, vanguard general, metropolitan commandant, with full staff.
proposals.after: Murong De named him Chao, made him Prince of Beihai, palace attendant, General of the Agile Cavalry, metropolitan commandant, with full staff.
proposals.reason: 驃騎大將軍 is General of the Agile Cavalry, not a ‘vanguard’ general.

proposals.before: De treated him with great courtesy, for the first time naming him Chao, enfeoffing him Prince of Beihai, appointing him palace attendant, chief general of the vanguard, colonel director of the retainers, opening an office and installing aides.
proposals.after: De treated him with great courtesy, for the first time naming him Chao, enfeoffing him Prince of Beihai, appointing him palace attendant, General of the Agile Cavalry, colonel director of the retainers, opening an office and installing aides.
proposals.reason: Literal likewise mistranslates 驃騎大將軍 as ‘vanguard’.

proposals.before: Chao also deeply grasped De’s intent: within he gave full joyful service; without he humbled himself to men of talent—thereupon inside and outside praised his beauty.
proposals.after: Chao also deeply grasped De’s intent: within he gave full joyful service; without he humbled himself to men of talent—thereupon inside and outside praised his excellence.
proposals.reason: 稱美 means praise of excellence/virtue, not physical beauty.

proposals.before: Later Murong Zhong held Qingzhou, Duan Hong Xu, and Gongsun Wulou mixed martial guard and palace cavalry roles at court.
proposals.after: Later Murong Zhong held Qingzhou, Duan Hong held Xu, and Gongsun Wulou mixed martial guard and palace cavalry roles at court.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic fuses person 段宏 with place 徐州 as ‘Duan Hong Xu’.

proposals.before: Murong Chao heard and never forgave him.
proposals.after: When Chao heard it he harbored rage and resentment, shown in word and face.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic invents lasting unforgiveness; Chinese 恚恨形於言色 means rage and resentment manifested in speech and countenance.

proposals.before: Murong Fa skipped the funeral; Murong Chao sent a rebuke.
proposals.after: When De died, Fa again did not go to mourning; Chao sent envoys to reproach him.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits 德死 and the repeated refusal marked by 又不奔喪.

proposals.before: General Feng Rong defected to Wei.
proposals.after: The Western Gentlemen-General Feng Rong fled to Wei.
proposals.reason: 西中郎將 is a specific office title, not the generic ‘General’ of the idiomatic rendering.

proposals.before: Duke Zhuang’s minister Qumi was torn apart—recorded in the Annals.
proposals.after: Qumi’s tearing is written in the Spring and Autumn.
proposals.reason: Chinese names only 渠彌 and 《春秋》; ‘Duke Zhuang’s minister’ is an invented English gloss.

proposals.before: Shizong when he capital at Qi also pitied that punishments missed the mean and sighed, forgetting food and sleep.
proposals.after: Shizong, when he made his capital at Qi, also pitied that punishments missed the mean and sighed, forgetting food and sleep.
proposals.reason: Literal English is ungrammatical (‘when he capital at Qi’) and needs a verb of establishing the capital.

proposals.before: Yao Xing held Murong Chao’s women hostage, demanding vassalage, the imperial musicians, or else a thousand southerners.
proposals.after: Yao Xing detained Murong Chao’s mother and wife, demanding vassalage, the Grand Music performers, or else a thousand Wu captives.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic collapses 超母妻 into vague “women” and omits that the hostages are specifically mother and wife.

proposals.before: Chao sent his vice director Zhang Hua and attendant for miscellaneous purposes Zong Zhengyuan to Chang’an, delivering a hundred twenty Grand Music performers to Yao Xing.
proposals.after: Chao sent his Vice Director Zhang Hua and Supervising Secretary Zong Zhengyuan to Chang’an, delivering a hundred twenty Grand Music performers to Yao Xing.
proposals.reason: 給事中 is the office Supervising Secretary, not the unnatural phrase “attendant for miscellaneous purposes.”

proposals.before: ‘Now the Zongzhang goes west—surely the surplus will return east; is this not the omen of fortune and disaster!’”
proposals.after: ‘Now the Zongzhang goes west—surely You Yu will return east; is this not the omen of fortune and disaster!’”
proposals.reason: 由餘 is the historical person You Yu, not “surplus”; the omen parallels music going west with You Yu’s eastward return.

proposals.before: ‘Now the Zongzhang goes west—surely the surplus will return east; is this not the omen of fortune and disaster!’”
proposals.after: ‘Now the Zongzhang goes west—surely You Yu will return east; is this not the omen of fortune and disaster!’”
proposals.reason: Same 由餘 mistranslation in the literal English; restore the personal name You Yu.

proposals.before: He rewarded the raiders with county duchies.
proposals.after: Chao reviewed the merits of the Suyu campaign and enfeoffed Huguti and the others as dukes of commanderies and counties.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops Chao, the Suyu-merit deliberation, and Huguti.

proposals.before: Another raid took Jinan’s governor and slaves.
proposals.after: He again sent Gongsun Gui and others with three thousand horse to raid Jinan, seized Governor Zhao Yuan, and carried off more than a thousand men and women.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic invents “slaves,” omits Gongsun Gui and Zhao Yuan, and erases the stated scale.

proposals.before: Liu Yu reached Dongguan; Murong Chao sent fifty thousand under Duan Hui and Helailu to Linqu.
proposals.after: That summer the royal army halted at Dongguan; Chao sent his left army Duan Hui, assistant-state Helailu, and six other generals with fifty thousand foot and horse to advance and hold Linqu.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits summer dating, left-army and Fuguo titles, six other generals, and foot-and-horse composition.

proposals.before: But from antiquity when begging aid, if you do not send a great minister you do not draw heavy troops—therefore Zhao’s thrice begging indentured no Chu army;
proposals.after: But from antiquity when begging aid, if you do not send a great minister you do not draw heavy troops—therefore Zhao petitioned thrice and Chu’s army did not come forth;
proposals.reason: “Indentured” is a clear mistranslation of the failed thrice-made request for Chu troops.

proposals.before: Soon Liu Yu ringed Guanggu.
proposals.after: Before long, Yu’s army surrounded the city on all sides.
proposals.reason: The Chinese of this sentence does not name Guanggu; idiomatic invents the place-name.

proposals.before: Yao Xing dispatched Yao Qiang with ten thousand men to Luoyang to reinforce Han Fan.
proposals.after: At that time Yao Xing sent his general Yao Qiang leading ten thousand foot and horse to follow Fan and join his general Yao Shao at Luoyang, merging troops to come to the rescue.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits Yao Shao and the follow-Fan / join-at-Luoyang structure present in the Chinese.

proposals.before: Murong Chao’s archers drove Zhang Gang back.
proposals.after: Chao grew angry, laid ambush crossbows and shot at him; he then withdrew.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic erases Chao’s anger and the ambush-crossbow detail.

proposals.before: Right Vice Director Zhang Hua and palace secretary Feng Kai were both captured by Yu’s army.
proposals.after: Right Vice Director Zhang Hua and the Palace Aide to the Censor-in-chief Feng Kai were both captured by Yu’s army.
proposals.reason: 中丞 is the Palace Aide to the Censor-in-chief, not a generic palace secretary.

proposals.before: In youth he had judgment and capacity; joy and anger did not show on his face; his wit was bright and hair splendid, his speech clear in debate.
proposals.after: In youth he had judgment and capacity; joy and anger did not show on his face; his spirit and wit were outstanding, his speech clear in debate.
proposals.reason: 機神秀髮 is an idiom for outstanding talent and presence, not a literal reference to splendid hair.

proposals.before: On that account, whether government was great or small, all was delegated to him; he thereupon became a founding assistant without [parallel] merit.
proposals.after: On that account, whether government was great or small, all was delegated to him; he thereupon became a founding assistant of unmatched merit.
proposals.reason: 佐命無勳 here functions as unmatched founding merit; the bracketed paraphrase leaves the English self-contradictory.

proposals.before: His grandfather Feng Jun was a general.
proposals.after: His grandfather Feng Quan was a general.
proposals.reason: 悛 is Quan, not Jun; the English personal name misspells the given name.

proposals.before: His grandfather was Jun, General Who Rouses Might.
proposals.after: His grandfather was Quan, General Who Rouses Might.
proposals.reason: 悛 is Quan; rendering the given name as Jun is a transliteration error.

proposals.before: Murong Chao squandered Murong De’s legacy, provoked Jin, and destroyed the state.
proposals.after: Murong Chao squandered Murong De’s legacy, drew in the enemy, and destroyed the state.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names Suyu and Daxian and ‘延敵’; it does not say Jin in this sentence, so ‘provoked Jin’ invents a polity not in the unit.

decisions.reason: In a negative clause, English 'or' correctly means that he informed neither his mother nor his wife; changing it to 'and' is less idiomatic without improving fidelity.

decisions.after: Murong Chao inherited an established realm and a hegemon's legacy, yet neglected government and justice, delighted in hunting, shut out loyal men, advanced flatterers, and alienated his meritorious kin. His predecessors' legacy soon collapsed and his house's reputation went unrestored: he lost Suyu and brought disaster upon himself, opened Daxian to the enemy, and ended with ruler and ministers captive and the ancestral temples in ruins.
decisions.reason: The proposal removes one unsupported polity name but still omits nearly the entire historian's judgment; the revision restores its concrete charges and consequences.
